page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor to minimize virtualization overhead.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core tests and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with large-block read and write operations also placing in the top 10%. The processor's support for AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions contributes to strong performance in physics simulations, software compilation, and database operations.

This server does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, meaning workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated graphics must rely on network-attached storage and CPU-based processing. However, the high resource density of DDR5 memory and dedicated EPYC cores offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive parallel processing tasks, avoiding the overhead of hyperthreading. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

The hpc7a.24xlarge is designed for high-performance computing workloads, including molecular modeling, weather forecasting, computational fluid dynamics, and large-scale software compilation. It is also well-suited for memory-intensive database operations, parallel data processing, and CPU-based large language model inference, where its high memory bandwidth and dedicated core allocation can be fully leveraged.
